children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start by understanding your situation:

Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you: Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?

(By "non-advanced education" I mean education up to and including A levels or equivalent qualifications, not university degree level courses.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education at the moment. He finished school but hasn't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in paid work, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work. He's just at home at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your own situation.

Are you currently living in the UK, and are you responsible for Alex (meaning you live with him and are responsible for his care)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives here with me. I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

First, do you or Alex receive any benefits that might be relevant, such as Income Support, Universal Credit, or any disability benefits for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in his own name or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me now read the official guidance to confirm the eligibility rules before making my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official guidance I've reviewed, I can now make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

According to the rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child **under 16** and you live in the UK. For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if your child is **under 20** and they stay in approved education or training.

The guidance also states that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

In Alex's situation:
- He is 17 years old
- He is NOT in approved education or training
- He is NOT working 24 hours or more a week (he's not working at all)

This creates an important question: The rules clearly cover children under 16, and children aged 16-19 who are in education or training. However, Alex falls into a category where he is 17, not in education or training, but also not working 24+ hours per week.

Let me ask one final clarifying question: Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or is he within 20 weeks of leaving education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he left school but he hasn't signed up with any careers service or anything like that. He's just been at home for a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your situation against the UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, I'm afraid you would be **ineligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

Here's why:

Child Benefit is automatically available for children under 16. For young people aged 16 to 19, Child Benefit can continue **only if** they remain in approved education or training (such as A-levels, vocational courses, or approved training programs).

Since Alex is 17 and is not currently in any approved education or training, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for the 16-19 age group.

There is a temporary extension that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education, but only if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. As Alex hasn't registered with any careers service and has been at home for a while, this extension wouldn't apply either.

**What could change this:**
- If Alex enrolls in approved education or training (such as college, A-levels, or an approved training course)
- If Alex registers with a careers service immediately, you might be able to claim for a limited 20-week period

If you have any questions about this assessment or would like to discuss Alex's options, please feel free to ask.
